record.title: A paired-replay study finds weak history signals for predicting when agent context compaction will hurt
record.summary: Pakhomov and Nijkamp use TRACE’s paired-replay corpus to test whether an agent’s pre-compaction history predicts the harm caused by summarizing that context. Across 590 harness-triggered boundaries from 275 trajectories on 147 AppWorld tasks, the prespecified contrast between histories with and without prior writes is a wide null (dU@3 −0.062; 95% interval −0.209 to +0.079); a naive “has written” label largely tracks trajectory phase. The best history-based trigger reaches held-out AUROC 0.66, below a same-boundary replay yardstick of 0.72. A frozen two-feature logistic trigger at 83.7% retention avoids 20.6% of positive-burden boundaries by count, but has no detected advantage on burden mass. The study does not establish a deployable compaction policy: it covers one agent/compressor, one AppWorld cohort and a 4,096-token window, and cannot compare with a token-budget rule at matched retention.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors analyze 590 harness-triggered compaction boundaries from 275 trajectories on 147 AppWorld tasks using paired replay before and after compaction, one minimax-m3 agent/compressor and a 4,096-token context.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The prespecified contrast between prior-write and read-only histories is a wide null, while the naive “has written” label mostly tracks trajectory phase.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The best reported history trigger has held-out AUROC 0.66 versus a same-boundary replicate yardstick of 0.72; a frozen two-feature trigger avoids 20.6% of positive-burden boundaries at 83.7% retention by count, but has no detected burden-mass advantage.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION_OF_SOURCE
claims.text: The study does not establish cross-model generality, a deployable compaction policy, or performance against a token-budget rule at matched retention.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction or test across different models, compressors or harnesses was performed.
The public observables omit ordered histories, token counts, compression ratio and summary text; matched-retention comparison to token-budget compaction is unavailable.

brief.importance_rationale: If replicated across agent harnesses, per-boundary prediction of compaction harm could change context-management policies and evaluation design for long-horizon agents. The consequence is meaningful but bounded: this paper reports weak signals in one model/compressor and one AppWorld cohort, with no demonstrated deployable trigger or cross-system transfer.
limitations: All performance figures are author-reported; the research desk did not independently reproduce the analysis.
The cohort contains one agent model, one compressor and one deliberately tight 4,096-token window, with harness-triggered boundaries only on AppWorld.
Each boundary uses three to five replays per arm and the paired harm outcome is noisy; the same-boundary replicate AUROC is 0.72 while three-class sign agreement is 0.55 (κ=0.28).
The public release omits ordered actions, token counts, compression ratio and summary text, preventing a matched-retention comparison with a token-budget policy.
The source reports no data redistribution permission and the cited repository revision had no license file; independent replication must use authorized data access and must not rehost the corpus.
Trigger frontiers are offline plug-in estimates over logged outcomes, not a deployable fitted policy or measured task-success/latency benefit.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report a wide null on the prespecified prior-write versus read-only dU@3 contrast (−0.062; 95% interval −0.209 to +0.079), and find the naive “has written” label mostly tracks trajectory phase. The best history-based trigger reaches held-out AUROC 0.66 [0.61, 0.70], compared with 0.72 [0.69, 0.75] for a same-boundary replicate yardstick. At 83.7% retained compaction opportunities, a frozen two-feature logistic trigger avoids 20.6% [15.6%, 25.6%] of positive-burden boundaries by count but shows no advantage on burden mass (−0.001 [−0.034, +0.035]). These estimates are paper-reported and partly post hoc.
technical.compute_or_cost: No operational cost, token savings, latency, task-completion advantage or matched-retention comparison against a token-budget policy is measured.
technical.demonstrated_result: The public preprint specifies a paired replay over 590 harness-triggered boundaries from 275 trajectories on 147 AppWorld tasks, using one minimax-m3 agent/compressor and a 4,096-token window. the research desk has not independently reproduced the analysis; performance results below are author-reported.
technical.implementation_status: Research preprint arXiv v1 dated 2026-10-06. No deployable trigger or production result is established.
technical.mechanism: At each TRACE compaction boundary, the authors replay the same task prefix under the full pre-compaction context and under the stored summary plus retained turn, then compare the next one to five actions. They score blocked calls, repeated/refetched calls and their union, and train history-based triggers to select boundaries where compaction should be deferred.
technical.novelty: Uses paired counterfactual replays at individual context-compaction boundaries to evaluate next-action process harm, then compares history-based timing triggers against both a random-rule expectation and a same-boundary reproducibility yardstick.
technical.regime: One harness-triggered context-compaction corpus: 590 boundaries from 275 of 294 trajectories on 147 AppWorld tasks; one minimax-m3 agent/compressor, 4,096-token context, three to five replays per arm/boundary and a next-action burden outcome. Agent-chosen compaction, other models/compressors and non-AppWorld tasks are outside scope.
technical.reproducibility: The paper documents the analysis and identifies a public TRACE repository revision, but says the underlying data cannot be redistributed and the repository had no license file. The analysis record is available on request; the research desk did not obtain or reproduce it.
technical.strongest_baseline: A same-boundary split-half replay is used as a noise/replicability yardstick, not a deployable policy. The trigger is compared with a uniform random-rule expectation at equal-weight compaction opportunities; the paper cannot evaluate a token-budget rule at matched retention because token counts are not released.

brief.title: A paired-replay study finds weak history signals for predicting when agent context compaction will hurt
brief.why_it_matters: Context compaction is often triggered by a global token threshold, but delaying it based on recent agent behavior only helps if the history predicts which boundaries will be harmed. This study reports weak prediction in one controlled corpus and shows that a simple “has written” signal can be confounded with trajectory phase. It gives agent-harness designers a counterfactual evaluation target, while leaving cross-model generality and matched-retention policy value unresolved.
